one_sentence: The measurement problem's infinite regress is structurally resolved only by a triadic unity of three distinct functions in one unified act.
executive_summary: This paper argues that the quantum measurement problem, formalized by von Neumann in 1932, remains unsolved because every proposed interpretation—Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, decoherence, objective collapse—fails to terminate the observer regress. Through a logical walkthrough and formal analysis, the paper demonstrates that the only non-self-defeating solution is a triadic composition: three distinct functions (generation, structure, actualization) operating as a single unified act. This structure, which the paper derives from first principles, matches the Christian theological concept of the Trinity (Father, Son, Spirit). The conclusion is that the measurement problem is not a physical puzzle but a structural one, and its resolution requires a triadic ontology.
short_summary: This is a formal paper addressing the quantum measurement problem. The core structural claim is that the von Neumann regress can only be terminated by a triadic unity of three distinct functions—generation, structure, and actualization—operating as a single act. The key evidence is a logical reductio showing that all other options (one operator, two operators, three separate operators, no collapse, collapse by fiat) are self-defeating. This matters because it provides a rigorous, non-theological derivation of a triadic structure that resolves a foundational problem in quantum mechanics.

prerequisite_reading: ISO-025: Triadic Unity in Quantum Foundations
follow_up_reading: FP-003: The Trinity as a Formal Structure
